All walkthroughs / Health organisation

Health organisation · Patient recordings

Remove names from a patient recording and release it

A recording of a cardiology consultation is brought in, and a pipeline removes the names and dates from it. A reviewer decides whether it may be released. A researcher then asks for access, and a program has to ask the same way a person does.

Devi
Data engineer in the Health organisation

How to read this page

  • Every step is one screen, or one moment, in a real run. The label under the title names where it happens, and the step reads in the same order each time: what is happening, the evidence, and then what to look for in it.
  • Screenshots are real pictures of the Munitas console, the web app that people open in a browser. Click any picture to enlarge it.
  • Every name of a person, patient or card holder in the example data is invented, and every screenshot is unedited apart from being cropped to the part that matters.

Words used on this page

Organisation
A company or hospital group that uses Munitas. Each organisation sees only its own data.
Department
A team inside an organisation that owns some of its data, such as Cardiology.
Dataset
A named collection of records, such as a table of patient admissions.
Version
One sealed state of a dataset. Changing the contents means making a new version, never editing an old one.
Sealed
Finished and closed for good, so that it can never be edited.
Access level
How restricted a dataset is. Raw is the most restricted, and nobody may read it without permission. Published is the most open.
Custodian
A person who holds the data custodian role, which allows deciding who may read data. A custodian decides for the departments they are an approver for.
Pipeline
A series of steps that Munitas runs on a dataset version, each step after the ones it depends on. The last step is a gate decision.
Run
One execution of an agent or a pipeline, started for a stated purpose.
Gate decision
The final step of a pipeline, where a person decides whether a dataset version may be released to a more open access level. The person who started the run may not decide it.
De-identification reviewer
A role that allows a person to review data from which identifying details have been removed, and to decide whether it may be released.
Request
A written ask to read one dataset for one stated purpose. The custodian of the department that owns the dataset decides it.
Purpose
The reason a person states for reading data. A lease covers that purpose only, unless the custodian chooses otherwise.
Lease
Permission, given by the custodian, to read one dataset for one stated purpose and for a limited time.
Agent
A program registered on Munitas, with a named owner, that Munitas runs on somebody’s behalf instead of a person reading data directly.
Container
An isolated environment, with no network access of its own, where Munitas runs an agent.
Open for annotation
An access level above Under review, where people who label data may work with it.

PART ONE

Devi signs in

Devi is a data engineer at a hospital group that uses Munitas. Everybody in the organisation signs in on the same page. Who signs in decides what the console shows afterwards: a person sees only the data that the person's own organisation owns.

1
Devi
Devi signs in
Munitas console · Sign in · /auth/login

Devi types an email address and a password. Devi's job title, data engineer, is fixed by the organisation and is not chosen at sign-in. It decides what the platform lets Devi do, including one thing it will not allow in Part Three.

The email field reads devi@health.example, and the yellow bar reads Nobody is signed in, because the picture is taken before Devi presses Sign in.
2
Devi
Devi's home page counts the organisation's data
Munitas console · Home · /

The home page counts four things for the Health organisation only: datasets, sealed versions, versions released for wider use, and versions held back. A dataset is a named collection of records. A version is one state of a dataset, and sealed means finished and closed for good.

The panel at the top left reads Devi, Data engineer, Organisation: health. The four tiles are Datasets, Sealed versions, Released for wider use and Held back.
PART TWO

Devi brings a recording in

A recording of a cardiology consultation says the patient's name aloud and carries the patient's voice, so it identifies a person from the moment it exists. Bringing it into Munitas takes three steps, always in the same order: register a name and an owner, upload the file, and seal it so that it can never be changed.

3
Devi
Devi opens the form for a new dataset
Munitas console · Bring a dataset in · /datasets/register

Registering a dataset names who owns it and where it came from. Nothing is readable yet. A department is a team inside an organisation that owns some of its data, and the form requires one.

Owned by reads Choose a department, and What access level? already reads Raw (the safe default). The access level says how restricted a dataset is, and Raw is the most restricted. Register is pale until the form is complete.
4
Devi
Devi names the dataset and chooses Cardiology as its owner
Munitas console · Bring a dataset in · /datasets/register

Devi types a name, chooses the Cardiology department, and ticks audio. Hartley is a custodian, a person who decides who may read a department's data, and an approver of Cardiology, the department that owns this recording. Any approver of a department can decide, and Hartley is the one here, so Hartley will decide who may read this recording.

Owned by reads Cardiology, and the access level still reads Raw (the safe default). Choosing a lower level would be a claim recorded under Devi's name, which the custodian would have to agree with.
5
Devi
A file that is not a real recording is rejected
Munitas console · Bring a dataset in · upload step

Devi first tries a file named probe.wav that is not built as a real recording. Munitas reads what a file contains and does not trust what it is called.

A red line reads 'probe.wav' is named as audio but could not be read as a wav file: file does not start with RIFF id. Seal this as version 1 stays pale.
6
Devi
A genuine recording uploads, and version 1 is sealed
Munitas console · Bring a dataset in · upload and seal

Devi uploads a real recording and seals it with the ordinary seal button. Sealing closes the version: nothing can be added to it, and nothing in it can change. A later fix becomes a new version. This dataset only shows the three steps. The next part registers a second one sealed in the way the pipeline needs.

Uploaded sits next to cardiology-consult-synthetic.wav with its size and length, and a green panel reads Sealed as version 1, 1 file. Nothing about it can change from here; a later upload becomes a new version.
PART THREE

A pipeline removes the names, and a reviewer decides

De-identification means finding and removing identifying details, such as names and dates of birth, from a recording. Munitas does it with a pipeline: a series of steps that it runs on a dataset version. Nothing the pipeline produces is released automatically. It ends at a decision that only one role, the de-identification reviewer, may make.

7
Devi
Devi uploads a second recording with its answer key
Munitas console · Bring a dataset in · upload step

A second dataset, also owned by Cardiology. Devi uploads the recording and an answer key, a file that lists every identifying detail in it. The answer key lets the pipeline's own work be checked afterwards and not taken on trust.

Two files are listed, cardiology-consult-synthetic.wav and cardiology-consult-synthetic.truth.json. Two seal buttons appear: Seal this as version 1 and Seal as recordings.
8
Devi
Devi seals it as recordings
Munitas console · Bring a dataset in · upload and seal

Seal as recordings reads each audio file as a recording and matches it with its answer key. The de-identification pipeline can only run on a version sealed this way.

The green panel reads Sealed as version 1, 1 recording the de-identification pipeline can read.
9
Devi
Devi starts the de-identification pipeline
Munitas console · Pipeline run · /pipeline-runs/<id>

A run is one execution of a pipeline. A worker starts reading the sealed version. The page updates itself as the steps progress.

The line under the heading reads Running now. This page updates itself. Steps lists Transcribe the recordings, Find the identifiers, Hand off for annotation and Remove the identifiers, each marked Not started. What happens next says that nothing has been decided or released.
10
Devi
All four steps finish
Munitas console · Pipeline run · /pipeline-runs/<id>

The pipeline turned the speech into text, found the identifying details, and removed them. Each step is real work with a real duration. The page then says that a reviewer must decide, and that the reviewer cannot be whoever started the run.

Each step is marked Done with its duration. The measurement reads pass: recall 1.000, 0 direct leaks, 0 quasi-identifier leaks, and a link reads Open the decision.
11
Devi
Devi cannot approve the result of Devi's own run
Munitas console · De-identification results · /gates/<id>

The last step of a pipeline is a gate decision: a person decides whether the result may be released to a more open access level. Here it would move the recording from Under review to Open for annotation, which cannot be undone. Devi started the run, so Devi may not decide it.

The state reads Waiting for a decision. The text above the buttons reads You started this run, so somebody else has to clear it, and both buttons are pale.
12
Hartley
Hartley is refused for a different reason
Munitas console · De-identification results · /gates/<id>

Hartley owns the recording's department, yet opens the same decision and is refused. Owning a department's data and reviewing what a pipeline did to it are two separate kinds of authority.

The panel reads Hartley, Data custodian for Cardiology, and the text above the buttons reads Clearing a de-identification result is not part of your role.
13
Imani
Imani, the de-identification reviewer, opens the decision
Munitas console · De-identification results · /gates/<id>

Imani holds the one role this screen is built for, the de-identification reviewer. The buttons are still pale, not because of Imani's role but because a decision needs a written reason.

The panel reads Imani, De-identification reviewer. The Why you decided this box is empty.
14
Imani
Imani writes a reason, and the buttons become active
Munitas console · De-identification results · /gates/<id>

The reason is kept with the decision. Whoever reads it later will not have the recording or the results in front of them, only Imani's own words.

The reason is filled in, and Release to open for annotation and Hold it back are both active.
15
Imani
Imani holds the recording back
Munitas console · De-identification results · /gates/<id>

The decision is recorded with its reason. The recording stays at its original, most restricted level, and nobody has to ask Imani later why it was not released.

The state reads Held back, Your decision reads Held back by Imani followed by the reason, and a notice at the bottom right reads Held back.
PART FOUR

A researcher asks, and a custodian decides

Sam is a researcher who wants to read the original recording that Devi sealed. Sam's role does not read data at the Raw level, so the recording's page asks what the data would be used for before it shows anything more.

16
Sam
Sam opens the recording and finds a request form
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

A request is a written ask to read one dataset for one stated purpose. The page offers a request form where a file would be, and says who decides.

Your access reads This is more sensitive than your role reads, so Hartley decides. The form asks for a purpose, a reason and a length of time.
17
Sam
Sam writes the purpose and the reason
Munitas console · Version detail · the request form

Sam states the purpose and why a less sensitive substitute would not do. Both are shown to whoever decides, and neither is kept private.

The purpose reads measure recall of the de-identification model before wider release, and the reason reads for arrhythmia detection study, comparing detected spans against the original audio.
18
Sam
The request goes to the custodian
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

Sam cannot approve the request, and nothing is readable yet. The page says who it is waiting on.

Your access reads Your request has gone to the person answerable for this data. Nothing is readable until they grant it.
19
Hartley
Hartley finds Sam's request waiting
Munitas console · Home · the custodian's home page

Hartley's home page lists the requests to read Cardiology's data. A request for a recording that Radiology owns would never appear here. The decisions below the request were made earlier, some of them while other walkthroughs were recorded.

Waiting for your decision counts 1. The card reads Sam (Researcher) wants to read the recording, with Raw, Sam's reason, and Granting gives Sam 24 hours, for this purpose only.
20
Hartley
Hartley grants the request
Munitas console · Home · after granting

Granting creates a lease, which is permission to read one dataset for one purpose and for a limited time. The request leaves the waiting list and moves into the history of decisions.

A notice at the bottom right reads Access granted to Sam (Researcher), and Waiting for your decision counts 0.
PART FIVE

A program asks for access, the way a person does

An agent is a program registered on Munitas, with a named owner, that Munitas runs on somebody's behalf. Registering an agent gives it no right to read data. When it needs a Raw dataset, its run waits until the custodian of the department that owns the dataset decides.

21
Devi
Devi opens the radiology triage agent
Munitas console · Agents · /agents

radiology-intake-triage ranks radiology documents so that the most urgent ones reach a human reviewer first. It belongs to Radiology, so the Radiology custodian decides what it may read, not Hartley.

The row reads radiology-intake-triage, the purpose Ranks radiology intake documents for human review, the department Radiology, and the newest version followed by sealed.
22
Devi
The agent's page shows its owner, its identity and its versions
Munitas console · Agent detail · /agents/<id>

An agent's code is kept as sealed versions, the same way a dataset is. When it runs, the agent acts under an identity of its own, shown here as its runtime identity.

Owned by reads Radiology, Runtime identity (principal) shows a name ending in -runtime, and the newest version carries the label active.
23
Devi
Devi prepares a new version of the agent's code
Munitas console · Agent detail · the upload form

Devi chooses a zip of a small project. The model field says none, because the code calls no AI model, and the only tool it may use is read_dataset_version. The list of tools is a declaration. What limits the agent is that every read it makes is still checked against the same rules as a person's.

Project (.zip) shows triage-agent.zip, Model shows none, and Tools it may call shows read_dataset_version.
24
Devi
The new version is sealed
Munitas console · Agent detail · Versions

The version is identified by a hash of its own code and is sealed on arrival. The platform runs it in a container, an isolated environment with no network access beyond its own requests for access. Older versions below come from earlier recordings.

The newest version is at the top with a Deploy button, and the version below it carries the label active.
25
Devi
Devi starts a run and is told that it must wait
Munitas console · Agent detail · Runs

After deploying the new version, Devi names a purpose for a run and chooses radiology-reports, a Raw dataset that Radiology owns. Munitas warns before the click, not after.

A notice reads deployed. The orange line reads This agent cannot read that dataset on its own (RAW). Starting will ask Okonjo, who looks after Radiology, to grant it access, in your name. The run waits until they decide, and the button reads Request access and start.
26
Devi
The run waits for permission
Munitas console · Agent detail · Runs

The run is recorded and goes nowhere until the custodian decides. That is not a failure. It is the same pause that a person's request would meet.

The top row carries the label waiting for data access and the line Waiting for a custodian to grant this agent access to the dataset. It starts on its own once they do.
27
Okonjo
Okonjo sees who asked and who will do the reading
Munitas console · Home · the custodian's home page

Okonjo is the custodian of the Radiology department. The request names both people involved: Devi asked, on behalf of the agent's own runtime identity, to read the Radiology dataset. Nothing from Cardiology appears in this list.

The card reads Devi asked for health-radiology-intake-triage-runtime to read radiology-reports v1 with Raw, says that the request was made automatically so the agent can run, and says Granting gives the runtime identity 4 hours, for this purpose only.
28
Devi
A second run has to ask again
Munitas console · Agent detail · Runs

Okonjo's grant covered one purpose and was not a standing credential. Devi starts a second run on the same dataset for another purpose, and it waits again. This is what Raw data always gets. Reviewed data, which is no longer Raw, can be granted more widely, as the Finance walkthrough shows.

A new row at the top reads waiting for data access and ends with second batch, separate from the first run below it.
29
Devi
Once Okonjo agrees, the runs finish
Munitas console · Agent detail · Runs

Okonjo grants the second request, which this page does not show as its own screen, and the waiting run resumes by itself. Under each green label is the text that the agent's code printed. The sample agent prints one fixed result.

The top rows read succeeded, with 0 tool calls, and show the agent's printed result, contains an unusually urgent phrase, flagged for a human reviewer first.
PART SIX

Other pipelines, and the platform's own health

The de-identification pipeline in Part Three is the one that Munitas offers. Anybody may register a different pipeline that ends in the same kind of decision, as the custom pipeline walkthrough shows. And behind every screen is Priya, who can see whether the parts of Munitas are healthy.

30
Devi
Devi opens the Pipelines page
Munitas console · Pipelines · /pipelines

The page lists pipelines that people in the organisation have registered, each with its owning department and version. A pipeline is registered the way an agent is: as sealed versions that are identified by their contents.

The columns read Pipeline, Department and Version. The built-in de-identification pipeline is not in this list, because it ships with Munitas.
31
Priya
Priya sees the parts of the system
Munitas console · Home · the platform administrator's home page

Priya is the platform administrator, who runs Munitas itself and holds no standing access to any patient data. Priya's home page lists every part of the system that this story relied on, such as the control plane, the policy engine and the workflow engine, each with what stops working if it goes down.

Each card names a part, such as Control plane or Policy engine, says what it does, and ends with If it is down: and the effect.
